standard_prerequisites.name: Perfect case of the evaluation map

standard_prerequisites.name: Internal hom from strictly perfect
standard_prerequisites.use: K^ or  represented by termwise duals.

core_obligations: The canonical map K = R SheafHom(O_X,O_X)  otimes ^L K -> R SheafHom(R SheafHom(K,O_X),O_X) = (K^ or )^ or  is an isomorphism by the internal-hom-evaluate lemma and its perfect case (proof lines 12949-12955).

Localize and assume K strictly perfect with representative E^*; by the Rhom-strictly-perfect lemma K^ or  is represented by the complex with terms (E^{-n})^ or  = SheafHom_{O_X}(E^{-n},O_X) in degree n, which are direct summands of finite free modules; hence K^ or  is perfect (proof lines 12956-12971).

The evaluation map M  otimes ^L K^ or  -> R SheafHom(K,M) is represented, after choosing F^* for M, by the map of complexes with terms  oplus  F^p  otimes  (E^{-q})^ or  ->  oplus  SheafHom_{O_X}(E^{-q},F^p); it reduces to the canonical iso F  otimes  SheafHom_{O_X}(E,O_X) -> SheafHom_{O_X}(E,F) for E a direct summand of a finite free module, which follows from the finite free case (proof lines 12972-13012).
proof_roadmap: Double duality from the evaluation map.
Evaluation iso reduced to the module-level free-case adjunction.
difficulty_reason: Double duality comes from the evaluation map and the perfect case of the evaluate-isom lemma; localizing and taking a strictly perfect representative, the Rhom-strictly-perfect lemma identifies K^ or  with the termwise dual complex, and the evaluation isomorphism reduces to the free-case tensor-hom adjunction for summands of finite free modules.
